reason: A lateral lobe of the labellum is a labellum lobe. Position is not kept, as with inner/outer tepal.
French form of R2851.

An ochreola is a small sheath at the base of a pedicel or flower cluster, made of fused bracts (Polygonaceae). An ochrea is the stipular sheath around the stem node. R2872 already maps 'ochreole' to inflorescence bract, so the two rules disagree.
Plural of R2853: ochreola is not ochrea.
Spelling variant of ochreola. See R2853.
Plural of the ocreola variant. See R2853.
The seed cone scale bears the ovules, so megasporophyll is a fair functional match. It is not strictly homologous in conifers, so confidence is low.
Hyphenated variant of R2857.
Plural of R2857.
'Knee' alone also means a bent node or geniculate part in grasses and bamboos. It is a pneumatophore only when it is a root knee.
Plural of R2860, with the same ambiguity.
A knee root is an upward-growing respiratory root, which is a pneumatophore.
The carpocephalum is the female receptacle of Marchantiales, which is the archegoniophore.
Singular of R2863.
The lateral nerves arising from the midrib (the primary vein) are the secondary leaf veins. The word 'primary' only means the main laterals.
Plural of R2865.

A flower bract subtends a perianth. A staminate scale in catkins (Betulaceae, Casuarina, Carex) is a bract or glume subtending a naked or reduced male flower, so inflorescence bract is closer. In conifers it is a microsporophyll.
Plural of R2867.

A perianth cup is a cup made of fused perianth parts. A hypanthium is receptacle or axis tissue that carries the perianth and stamens, so the two are not the same. Perianth tube or calyx tube is closer.
An umbellate raceme is a raceme with an umbel-like look. The base class is acceptable, though the umbellate detail is lost.
The fruiting axis is the axis of the infructescence.
The ochreole (ochreola) of Polygonaceae is a bract-derived sheath on the inflorescence or pedicel.
Hyphenated spelling of spathe tube.
The leaf face is the leaf surface (upper or lower), and the lamina epidermis is the surface layer. Phyllodes and needles are the exceptions.
Plural of R2874.
'Faces' alone also means the faces of a petal, seed, valve, glume or achene.
The anther theca is the half-anther with two pollen sacs. The French spelling without an accent is the same word.
French 'thèque de l'anthère' is the anther theca.
Plural of R2878.
In gymnosperm ovules the pollen chamber is a cavity at the top of the nucellus that receives pollen. That is not a pollen sac. It is a pollen sac only in anthers.
The 'loge pollinique' is the anther locule, which is the pollen sac.
Plural of R2881.
A polychasium is a compound cyme with many lateral branches. The cyme class is the nearest existing term.
The PO comment treats the alar region as the area of alar cells. The loss of 'region' is minor.
Direct match.
A cone scale is a sporophyll, or sporophyll-like, in cones. It is homologous only in some groups, so confidence is limited.
Plural of R2886.
Stigmatic rays are the ray-like lobes of the stigma, for example in Papaver.
Plural of R2888.
Variant of R2888.
The floret tube is the corolla tube in Asteraceae and similar heads. In grasses the floret has no such tube.
Plural of R2891.
A fertile bract is a bract that bears flowers. 'Fertile' is dropped, as with inner and outer tepal.
French form of R2893.
Plural of R2894.
The inner tepal is a tepal. The review of 2026-11-13 already mapped 'inner tepal' to tepal.
French form of R2896.
Plural of R2897.
A male floret is a staminate flower (a staminate floret in Poaceae and Asteraceae).
A pappus hair is a bristle-like pappus element.
